drafts.title: Riccarton RFC Fundraiser Health and Safety Plan

sections.heading: Hazard identification, assessment, control and review
sections.body: A system will be implemented to identify, assess, control, and review hazards before and during the Riccarton RFC Fundraiser. This includes regular inspections and risk assessments of the site at Hagley Park. Identified hazards such as cooking on site, the use of generators, and the presence of inflatables will be assessed for risk. Controls will be put in place to mitigate these risks, such as ensuring all electrical equipment is properly installed and maintained, and inflatables are securely anchored. A review process will be conducted throughout the event to ensure ongoing safety.

sections.heading: Health and safety responsibilities
sections.body: Health and safety responsibilities will be assigned to specific staff members and volunteers. [HEALTH AND SAFETY OFFICER NAME] will oversee the implementation of the health and safety plan. Volunteers will be briefed on their specific responsibilities, including monitoring crowd safety and ensuring compliance with safety protocols.

sections.heading: Staff competency and supervision
sections.body: All staff and volunteers will be required to demonstrate the necessary knowledge and skills for their roles. Those lacking experience will be supervised by more experienced personnel. Training sessions will be conducted prior to the event to ensure everyone is adequately prepared.

sections.heading: Pre-event site inspection
sections.body: A comprehensive site inspection will be conducted at Hagley Park prior to the event. This inspection will ensure that all structures, including marquees and inflatables, are safely erected and that the site is free from hazards. [INSPECTION TEAM LEADER NAME] will lead this inspection.

sections.heading: Accident register
sections.body: An accident register will be maintained on site to record any incidents that occur during the event. This register will be reviewed regularly to identify any patterns or recurring issues that need addressing.

sections.heading: Emergency plan
sections.body: An emergency plan specific to the Riccarton RFC Fundraiser will be in place. This plan will cover potential emergencies such as fire, medical incidents, and severe weather. Emergency procedures will be communicated to all staff and volunteers, and emergency contact numbers will be readily available.

sections.heading: Health and safety briefings
sections.body: Documented health and safety briefings will be conducted for all staff and volunteers before each session of the event. These briefings will cover emergency procedures, hazard awareness, and individual responsibilities. Attendance will be recorded to ensure compliance.

sections.heading: Working with partners and suppliers
sections.body: Collaboration with partners and suppliers will be essential to ensure public safety. All suppliers will be required to adhere to the health and safety standards set for the event. Regular communication will be maintained to address any safety concerns that arise.

drafts.title: Waste Management Confirmation for Riccarton RFC Fundraiser

sections.heading: How waste will be managed
sections.body: The organiser will ensure that all waste generated during the Riccarton RFC Fundraiser at Hagley Park is collected and disposed of appropriately. Waste management will involve setting up designated waste collection points throughout the event site to encourage proper disposal by attendees.

sections.heading: Types and amounts of waste
sections.body: As the event is expecting fewer than 1000 attendees, a detailed estimate of the types and amounts of waste is not required. However, it is anticipated that waste will primarily consist of food packaging, beverage containers, and general litter from the food stalls and beer tent.

sections.heading: Waste minimisation
sections.body: Although not required for this event size, the organiser is encouraged to implement waste minimisation strategies such as using recyclable materials and encouraging vendors to minimise packaging.

sections.heading: Landfill diversion target
sections.body: A specific landfill diversion target is not required for this event size. However, the organiser is encouraged to aim for a high rate of recycling and composting to reduce landfill waste.

sections.heading: Collection equipment
sections.body: The organiser will provide bins for general waste, recycling, and composting at various locations around the event site to facilitate waste collection and separation.

sections.heading: Who is responsible
sections.body: The responsibility for waste collection and disposal lies with the event organiser. The organiser will need to confirm the individual or company responsible for this task.

sections.heading: Collection schedule
sections.body: The organiser will need to establish a schedule for waste collection during the event. This should include regular checks and emptying of bins to prevent overflow.

sections.heading: Litter and spillages
sections.body: The organiser will ensure that litter and spillages are promptly managed by having staff or volunteers regularly patrol the event area to clean up any waste or spills.

drafts.title: Hazard Register for Riccarton RFC Fundraiser

sections.heading: Activity
sections.body:
1. Setting up and dismantling marquees and inflatables.
2. Operating food stalls with on-site cooking.
3. Managing the beer tent area where alcohol is sold.
4. Use of generators for power supply.
5. Amplified sound equipment operation.

sections.heading: Hazards
sections.body:
1. Personal injury from lifting heavy equipment or structures.
2. Burns or fire hazards from cooking equipment.
3. Alcohol-related incidents in the beer tent.
4. Electric shock from generators.
5. Hearing damage from loud amplified sound.

sections.heading: Persons at risk
sections.body:
1. Event staff and volunteers.
2. Attendees, including children.
3. Food stall operators.
4. Performers and sound technicians.

sections.heading: Risk before control measures (severity x likelihood)
sections.body:
1. Personal injury: Severity 3 x Likelihood 3 = 9
2. Burns/fire: Severity 4 x Likelihood 3 = 12
3. Alcohol incidents: Severity 3 x Likelihood 4 = 12
4. Electric shock: Severity 4 x Likelihood 2 = 8
5. Hearing damage: Severity 3 x Likelihood 3 = 9

sections.heading: Controls
sections.body:
1. Provide manual handling training and use of lifting equipment.
2. Fire extinguishers and fire blankets at each cooking station.
3. Designated sober supervisors in the beer tent.
4. Regular inspection and maintenance of electrical equipment.
5. Limit sound levels and provide ear protection for staff.

sections.heading: Residual risk after control measures
sections.body:
1. Personal injury: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
2. Burns/fire: Severity 3 x Likelihood 2 = 6
3. Alcohol incidents: Severity 2 x Likelihood 3 = 6
4. Electric shock: Severity 3 x Likelihood 1 = 3
5. Hearing damage: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4

sections.heading: Additional controls
sections.body:
1. Monitor and review manual handling practices.
2. Conduct fire drills with staff.
3. Regularly review alcohol management policies.
4. Schedule regular electrical safety checks.
5. Monitor sound levels throughout the event.

sections.heading: Owner
sections.body:
1. [EVENT SAFETY OFFICER NAME] for manual handling and electrical safety.
2. [FIRE SAFETY OFFICER NAME] for fire safety.
3. [ALCOHOL MANAGEMENT OFFICER NAME] for alcohol-related controls.
4. [SOUND TECHNICIAN NAME] for sound level management.

drafts.title: Alcohol Management Plan for Riccarton RFC Fundraiser

sections.heading: Type of event
sections.body: The Riccarton RFC Fundraiser is a public event held at Hagley Park on 14 March 2027, from 12:00 to 19:00. The event is expected to attract up to 400 attendees, including children. Alcohol will be sold in a designated beer tent for adults. The event's risks include managing intoxication, ensuring minors do not consume alcohol, and maintaining a safe environment for families.

sections.heading: Promoting your event
sections.body: Pre-event communication will include information on alcohol restrictions, age limits, and expected behaviour. This will be disseminated through event promotions and signage at the venue.

sections.heading: Intoxication
sections.body: Procedures will be established to monitor patrons and prevent intoxication. Staff will be trained to identify early signs of intoxication and intervene appropriately. A designated safe place will be identified for patrons who become intoxicated.

sections.heading: Food
sections.body: [FOOD RESPONSIBLE PERSON] will ensure that food is available at all times while alcohol is sold. Three food stalls will be present, and food options will be promoted throughout the event.

sections.heading: Low and non-alcohol beverages
sections.body: [BEVERAGE RESPONSIBLE PERSON] will ensure a reasonable range of low and non-alcohol beverages is available at all times. Free water will be readily available and promoted to all patrons.

sections.heading: Minors
sections.body: ID checks will be conducted for anyone appearing under 25 years of age. Acceptable forms of identification will include a passport, New Zealand driver's licence, or HANZ 18+ card.

sections.heading: Signage
sections.body: Signage will be displayed at each point of sale, including the licence and prohibited-person signage. This will ensure compliance with legal requirements.

sections.heading: Safe transport
sections.body: Safe transport options will be promoted, including public transport and taxi services. Information will be displayed prominently at the event, and staff will assist patrons in arranging transport if needed.

sections.heading: Alcohol promotions on the day
sections.body: Promotions will not encourage excessive drinking. No discounts or offers will be made that could lead to excessive consumption.

sections.heading: Staff training
sections.body: All staff will receive training on host responsibility, the conditions of the special licence, and procedures for managing intoxication and minors. Training will occur before the event.

sections.heading: Incident and noting book
sections.body: An incident and noting book will be maintained to record any issues related to patron behaviour, refusals of service, and other relevant incidents. [INCIDENT BOOK RESPONSIBLE PERSON] will manage this.

sections.heading: Security
sections.body: Certified security staff will be employed to manage the crowd, given the expected attendance of 400 patrons. [SECURITY FIRM NAME] will provide security services, and [SECURITY RESPONSIBLE PERSON] will liaise with them.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.body: The event will provide a relaxed atmosphere with appropriate lighting, seating, and entertainment. Drinking games and activities promoting excessive alcohol consumption are prohibited. Adequate toilet facilities will be available.

sections.heading: Debriefing
sections.body: A debriefing session will be held with staff and contractors after the event to identify areas for improvement. Feedback from Police, Council, and Health may be included if necessary.

items.text: Each row describes the activity and how it could pose a risk
items.evidence:
1. Setting up and dismantling marquees and inflatables.
2. Operating food stalls with on-site cooking.
3. Managing the beer tent area where alcohol is sold.
4. Use of generators for power supply.
5. Amplified sound equipment operation.

items.text: Each row names the hazards (e.g. injury, electric shock, falls from height, crushing)
items.evidence:
1. Personal injury from lifting heavy equipment or structures.
2. Burns or fire hazards from cooking equipment.
3. Alcohol-related incidents in the beer tent.
4. Electric shock from generators.
5. Hearing damage from loud amplified sound.

items.text: Each row describes controls that reduce the risk to a tolerable or acceptable rating
items.evidence:
1. Provide manual handling training and use of lifting equipment.
2. Fire extinguishers and fire blankets at each cooking station.
3. Designated sober supervisors in the beer tent.
4. Regular inspection and maintenance of electrical equipment.
5. Limit sound levels and provide ear protection for staff.

items.text: Defines the type of event and its risks
items.evidence: The Riccarton RFC Fundraiser is a public event held at Hagley Park on 14 March 2027, from 12:00 to 19:00. The event is expected to attract up to 400 attendees, including children. Alcohol will be sold in a designated beer tent for adults. The event's risks include managing intoxication, ensuring minors do not consume alcohol, and maintaining a safe environment for families.

items.text: Pre-event communication covers intoxication, alcohol restrictions, age limits and behaviour
items.evidence: Pre-event communication will include information on alcohol restrictions, age limits, and expected behaviour. This will be disseminated through event promotions and signage at the venue.

items.text: Sets procedures to monitor patrons and prevent intoxication
items.evidence: Procedures will be established to monitor patrons and prevent intoxication. Staff will be trained to identify early signs of intoxication and intervene appropriately.

items.suggestedFix: Specify the location or description of the designated safe place for intoxicated patrons.

items.suggestedFix: [BEVERAGE RESPONSIBLE PERSON] will ensure a reasonable range of low and non-alcohol beverages is available at all times.

items.evidence: Free water will be readily available and promoted to all patrons.

items.evidence: ID checks will be conducted for anyone appearing under 25 years of age. Acceptable forms of identification will include a passport, New Zealand driver's licence, or HANZ 18+ card.

items.evidence: Signage will be displayed at each point of sale, including the licence and prohibited-person signage.

items.text: Promotions do not encourage excessive drinking
items.evidence: Promotions will not encourage excessive drinking. No discounts or offers will be made that could lead to excessive consumption.

items.text: All staff are trained and briefed before the event
items.evidence: All staff will receive training on host responsibility, the conditions of the special licence, and procedures for managing intoxication and minors. Training will occur before the event.
